fix: In 'tube ..., twisted; lobes ..., not twisted' the negation belongs to the part named right before it in the same clause (here 'lobes'), not to the whole organ. Bear it on the sub-part.
reason: The flora calls the corolla tube twisted and the lobes not twisted. 'Corolla not twisted' clashes with 'tube twisted'.

fix: In '<shape> with long tapering tips', 'tapering' describes the tips. Bear it on the apex (leaf apex), not on the whole leaf.
reason: The leaf is lanceolate-ovate. Only its tips taper.
Nutlet ca. 4 × 3 mm: the width is 3 mm. A nutlet is a fruit.
'Summer-green' means the fronds die back in winter, so the plant is deciduous.
The genus is perennial or biennial, rarely annual. Annual is one of the life spans the flora lists for the taxon.
The lowest involucral bract is said to be not sheathing. Bract is an acceptable bearer.
Seeds are 0.5-0.8 mm. A single dimension is read as length.
The fruits are described as claw-shaped.
Rounded lower-lip lobes are read as obtuse, which follows the reviewed rule. The container (lip) is kept.
'Wingless' is 'winged' negated, on the seed.
Blade 1.5-2 x 0.4-0.8 cm: the width is 0.4-0.8 cm.
½ to 1½ feet is 15.24 to 45.72 cm, the plant's height.
The leaves are simple ('Feuilles ... simples').
Young branchlets are smooth, and the 'young' slot is set. ('Non-lenticellate' and 'deciduous' are separate statements.)

fix: In a leaf series ('proximal ... lobes 14–30; distal ... lobes 10–26'), each count must keep the position word (distal, proximal) that opens its clause as a bearer context.
reason: 10–26 lobes is said only of the distal leaves. The leaves before them have 14–30, so the count without a position is false for the leaves as a whole.
The lower stem-leaves are linear-lanceolate. The 'lower' slot (FLOPO_0991377) is kept, and lanceolate is an acceptable broader reading.
Young fruit brown, with the 'young' context.
Pedicels are 0.4–1.5 cm at the flowering stage. The stage slot is set, which keeps this apart from the fruiting length of 1–2 cm.
(1–)1.5–5 dm is 15–50 cm, with a low extreme of 10 cm. Herb height.
The ovary is adnate to the floral disc. 'Lower part' narrows this but does not make the annotation false.
In Aconitum, a galeate (helmet-shaped) upper sepal is the hooded, cucullate form. No galeate class exists.
The stigmas are spirally coiled.

target: acute (FLOPO_0991095) or acuminate (PATO_0002228); bearer at apex
fix: In 'X or Y-Z', a hyphenated compound (obtuse-acuminate) is one value. Do not cut it to its first word. Ground the compound to its head (acuminate), or leave it ungrounded, and keep the 'at apex' place.
reason: The second option is 'obtuse-acuminate', not 'obtuse'. Also, the shape is said of the lobe apex.
The lamina base is attenuate into the petiole.
Each umbel has 4–10 flowers. The inflorescence container is set.

fix: In drupe descriptions, 'stone' means the pyrene (endocarp plus seed), not the seed. Map 'stone(s)' to pyrene.
reason: The stones of the drupe are not flattened. That says nothing directly about the seed.

target: container: panicle branch; position: shorter branches
fix: In 'branches ..., shorter with N spikelets, longer with M spikelets', the count is per branch and depends on which branch. Keep the container (branch) and the position (shorter or longer).
reason: 3–6 spikelets is said of the shorter panicle branches. The longer ones have 6–9, and the panicle as a whole has many more.
The pod (fruit) is 1.5 cm long.
'Oblong-ovate' is fairly read as a shape between oblong and ovate. 'Lingulate' is a separate alternative, outside this annotation.
Racemes are up to 10 cm long in fruit. The upper bound and the fruiting stage are both set.
